disease_label_per_paper: Disseminated gonococcal infection (Neisseria gonorrhoeae bacteremia) with acute hepatitis, without Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome
presentation_summary: 31-year-old man presented to the emergency department with 4 days of epigastric pain after a recent out-of-state vacation with several new sexual contacts; since return he had fever up to 38.5 C, nausea, penile discharge, and diarrhea.
He reported no arthritic or dermatologic symptoms. In the emergency department he was tachycardic, tachypneic, and febrile.

Labs: total bilirubin 7.8 mg/dL, conjugated bilirubin 5.9 mg/dL, AST 8520 U/L, ALT 5814 U/L, ALP 212 U/L, total protein 6.3, albumin 3.6, WBC and hemoglobin within normal limits, sodium 131 mmol/L, creatinine 1.42 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL), venous pH 7.29, lactate 9.6 mmol/L. Urinalysis showed bilirubin, protein, leukocytes, and white blood cell casts.
CT chest/abdomen/pelvis: enlarged steatotic liver and mild stranding around the bladder and appendix.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Urgent care respiratory/pharyngeal PCR panel negative before presentation
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Negative PCR for Group A Strep, Covid-19, Influenza A, Influenza B, and Respiratory Syncytial Virus (Table 1, T = -2d)

confirmatory_findings.finding: Urgent care STI testing (collected T=-1d, resulted hospital day 1): Neisseria gonorrhoeae RNA positive and Chlamydia trachomatis RNA positive
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Overnight, his sexually transmitted infection screening from urgent care came back remarkable for a positive Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis RNA result.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Blood culture positive for Neisseria gonorrhoeae (1 of 2 sets, hospital day 2); repeat blood cultures negative
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: On day 2 of hospitalization, one of his two sets of blood cultures returned positive for Neisseria gonorrhoeae ... These repeat blood cultures remained negative

confirmatory_findings.finding: Viral hepatitis and other viral exclusion serologies
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: He was noted to have a negative hepatitis B and hepatitis C antibody screen. His hepatitis A immunoglobulin G (IgG) was positive, but hepatitis A immunoglobulin M (IgM) was negative ... his hepatitis E IgM, cytomegalovirus PCR, Epstein-Barr virus, and adenovirus IgM returned unremarkable. He was noted to have a positive adenovirus IgG.

confirmatory_findings.finding: MRCP (hospital day 1): hepatomegaly, moderate hepatic steatosis, perihepatic ascites, periportal edema; no hepatic capsule distention, capsule adhesions, or hepatic abscess
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography was performed, which confirmed hepatomegaly with a moderate degree of hepatic steatosis, perihepatic ascites, and periportal edema but no evidence of hepatic capsule distention, hepatic capsule adhesions, or hepatic abscesses.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Final attribution: acute hepatitis secondary to disseminated gonococcal infection; Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome not supported
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Given his positive blood cultures for Neisseria gonorrhoeae and his otherwise unremarkable workup, his acute hepatitis was suspected to be secondary to disseminated gonococcal infection.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Hepatic panel trend after admission and treatment response
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Table 2: 10/14/24 17:04 T bili 7.0, AST 8,774, ALT 6,073; 10/15/24 AST 6,616, ALT 5,540; ... 10/21/24 T bili 11.4, AST 156, ALT 733; 12/04/24 T bili 0.8, AST 37, ALT 26. His liver function tests, lactic acidosis, acute kidney injury, and abdominal pain continued to improve on this antibiotic regimen

actual_treatment: ceftriaxone 1 g daily (14 days from last negative blood culture)
PrEP (emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate) held during admission, later restarted

outcome.source_text_value: on day 4 of hospitalization he was deemed stable for discharge home ... approximately 5 months post discharge, and all components of the hepatic function panel were found to be within normal limits.

quality_warnings: Emergency department heart rate, respiratory rate and temperature were reported only qualitatively (tachycardic, tachypneic, febrile); body_temperature uses the pre-presentation maximum of 38.5 C.
Total protein and albumin come from the paper's Table 2 image, which lists no units; g/dL assumed.
Microbiology (gonococcal/chlamydial NAAT, blood culture), exclusion serologies, day-1 MRCP, treatment, and outcome are retained as non-ranking context.
Classic DGI arthritis-dermatitis features were explicitly absent and are kept as rankable negative evidence.
